findings.description: For a command with no Argument parameters, all() over an empty list returns True, so the 'Positional arguments' section heading is written even though there is nothing to list. The original `if args:` guard is gone.
findings.rationale: Trigger: any command that defines only options (no arguments), which is very common. args is [], all(...) is True, so formatter.section(...) runs and writes the heading. HelpFormatter.section writes the heading unconditionally, and write_dl with no rows adds nothing. Impact: every such command's --help output gains an empty 'Positional arguments:' heading, a visible regression on a common path.

findings.description: The section is suppressed entirely when any argument lacks help, because the check requires all arguments to be documented. The docstring says the section is written 'if at least one is documented', and the new comment says undocumented arguments get an empty description.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a command with two arguments where only one has help=..., for example @click.argument('src', help='source') plus @click.argument('dst'). all() is False, so no Positional arguments section is written and neither argument is listed. Impact: --help hides documented arguments, the opposite of the stated intent of listing every argument, and the behavior contradicts the docstring.
